explain.say: Before 1956, workers loaded ships by hand, sack by sack. It took days and cost a lot. Then an American trucking boss, Malcom McLean, put 58 metal boxes on a ship called the Ideal X. The boxes went from truck to ship without being unpacked. Can you see why that was faster?

faq.a: Malcom McLean, an American trucking businessman, started modern container shipping in 1956 when the Ideal X carried 58 containers from Newark to Houston.

faq.q: Why are all containers the same size?
faq.a: In the late 1960s countries agreed international standard sizes, mostly 20 and 40 feet long. So any crane, ship, train or truck can handle any container. Ship sizes are counted in TEU, twenty-foot equivalent units.

faq.q: Which is the busiest port in the world?
faq.a: Shanghai in China has been the world’s busiest container port since 2010, handling tens of millions of containers a year. Singapore is usually second.
asks: Where is the biggest container port?

faq.q: What happened when the Suez Canal was blocked?
faq.a: In March 2021 the huge ship Ever Given got stuck across the Suez Canal in Egypt for six days. Hundreds of ships had to wait, because about 12 percent of world trade passes through the canal.

faq.q: How did containers change the world?
faq.a: Containers made shipping much cheaper and faster, so companies could make goods wherever it cost least and ship them anywhere. This helped create today’s global supply chains.
asks: Why are so many things made in China?

facts: The Ideal X carried 58 containers from Newark to Houston on 26 April 1956.
Shanghai has been the world's busiest container port since 2010.
In March 2021 the Ever Given blocked the Suez Canal for six days.
